topic: Tardigrades surviving open space (ESA FOTON-M3 2007) and 30-year freeze revival
hook: Tardigrades survived 10 days in open space
tag_reason: ESA flew the tardigrades on its FOTON-M3 mission
caption:
In 2007, tiny animals called tardigrades rode on the outside of an ESA spacecraft for 10 days, exposed to vacuum and cosmic radiation. Many came home alive, and some even laid eggs.

Their trick is drying out almost completely. Others frozen in Antarctic moss for 30 years woke up and had babies. Follow @you.didnot.know for one verified fact you can't unlearn, every day.

Would you rather be able to survive space or survive 30 years frozen?

1/4 The 2007 space test (10 d)
In 2007, ESA flew dried tardigrades outside a capsule in orbit, exposed to space vacuum and cosmic radiation.
📷 Schokraie E, Warnken U, Hotz-Wagenblatt A, Grohme MA, Hengherr S, et al. (2012) (CC BY 2.5) via wikimedia

2/4 Dried into a 'tun' (tun)
They survive by losing almost all their body water and curling into a 'tun'. Their metabolism nearly stops.
🎨 AI-generated image

3/4 Some survived raw sunlight (1000x)
Most died under full solar UV, over 1,000 times Earth's surface level. A few survived and later laid eggs.
📷 European Space Agency (CC BY-SA 3.0 igo) via wikimedia

4/4 Back after 30 years (30 yr)
Tardigrades frozen in Antarctic moss since 1983 woke up in 2014 and went on to reproduce.
📷 NOAA Photo Library (Public domain) via wikimedia
